# Digital Worlds Lab

> Free money calculators, plain-language budgeting guides with worked examples, and budget / debt payoff / savings / self-employed spreadsheet templates for Google Sheets and Excel. Euro-friendly (any currency), with Polish and German pages. Made by Digital Worlds Lab, a small independent studio. Calculators are free with no sign-up; templates are sold on Etsy (https://digitalworldslab.etsy.com) and Gumroad (https://digitallab8.gumroad.com).

## Free calculators (no sign-up)

- [Etsy Digital Download Fee Calculator (2026) – Free](https://digitalworlds.cc/calculator/): Free Etsy fee calculator for digital downloads and physical items: listing fee, 6.5% transaction fee, payment processing and Offsite Ads. See your real profit per sale and the price you need.
- [50/30/20 Budget Calculator – Free, Monthly or Yearly](https://digitalworlds.cc/budget-calculator/): Free 50/30/20 budget calculator. Enter your take-home pay and see how much goes to needs, wants and savings or debt, then compare with what you spend now.
- [Debt Snowball vs Avalanche Calculator – Free Payoff Date](https://digitalworlds.cc/debt-snowball-calculator/): Free debt snowball and avalanche calculator. Add your debts, choose a method and an extra monthly payment, and see your debt-free date, payoff order and total interest.
- [Sinking Funds Calculator – How Much to Save Each Month](https://digitalworlds.cc/sinking-funds-calculator/): Free sinking funds calculator. List what you are saving for (Christmas, car repairs, vacation, insurance), the amount and the date, and see exactly how much to save each month or paycheck.
- [Wedding Budget Calculator – Breakdown by Category](https://digitalworlds.cc/wedding-budget-calculator/): Free wedding budget calculator. Enter your total budget and guest count to see a typical breakdown by category (venue, catering, photography, attire, flowers and more) and your cost per guest.
- [Self-Employed Tax Calculator – How Much to Set Aside (US, 1099)](https://digitalworlds.cc/self-employed-tax-calculator/): Free self-employed tax calculator for US freelancers and 1099 workers. Estimate self-employment tax, income tax set-aside and quarterly estimated payments from your profit.
- [How Much House Can I Afford? Calculator by Take-Home Pay](https://digitalworlds.cc/house-affordability-calculator/): Free house affordability calculator based on take-home pay: see a comfortable and a stretch home price, monthly payment and loan size from your income, debts, deposit and mortgage rate.
- [Rent vs Buy Calculator: Is Renting Cheaper Than Owning?](https://digitalworlds.cc/rent-vs-buy-calculator/): Free rent vs buy calculator. Compare your rent with the true yearly cost of owning: mortgage interest, property tax, maintenance and the lost return on your deposit. Find your break-even rent.
- [How Much Car Can I Afford? 20/4/10 Rule Calculator](https://digitalworlds.cc/car-affordability-calculator/): Free car affordability calculator using the 20/4/10 rule: 20% down, a loan of 4 years or less, and total car costs under 10% of gross income. Check a car price or find your maximum.
- [Free Embeddable Money Calculators for Your Blog](https://digitalworlds.cc/embed/): Nine free money calculators you can embed on any blog or website with one line of code: debt snowball, sinking funds, 50/30/20 budget, Etsy fees, wedding budget, rent vs buy and more. No sign-up, no ads.

## Guides with worked examples

- [Money Guides: Budgeting, Debt and Savings](https://digitalworlds.cc/guides/): Plain guides to budgeting, paying off debt, sinking funds and self-employed tax, with free calculators and worked examples.
- [Debt Snowball vs Avalanche: Which Pays Off Debt Faster? (Worked Example)](https://digitalworlds.cc/guides/debt-snowball-vs-avalanche/): A worked example with four real-looking debts: how the debt snowball and debt avalanche methods compare on months, interest and payoff order.
- [50/30/20 Budget Rule: A Simple Example With Real Numbers](https://digitalworlds.cc/guides/50-30-20-budget-example/): How the 50/30/20 budget works, with a worked example on a €2,800 monthly take-home pay, what counts as needs and wants, and what to do if your needs are over 50%.
- [Sinking Funds List: 15 Categories and How Much to Save Each Month](https://digitalworlds.cc/guides/sinking-funds-list/): A practical sinking funds list with 15 common categories and the simple formula for how much to set aside each month, so big expenses stop wrecking your budget.
- [How Much to Set Aside for Taxes When Self-Employed (US, 2026)](https://digitalworlds.cc/guides/self-employed-tax-set-aside/): How US self-employment tax works in 2026, a worked example of what to set aside from each payment, and a simple system for quarterly estimated taxes.
- [How to Make a Christmas Budget (With a Gift List Example)](https://digitalworlds.cc/guides/christmas-budget/): A simple Christmas budget in four steps: set one total, split it into gifts, food, travel and extras, list every person, and track as you shop. Worked example with a €900 budget.
- [Holiday Money Guides 2026–2027](https://digitalworlds.cc/holiday/): Practical money guides for the holidays and the new year: pricing for Christmas markets, a January budget reset, saving €10k in 2027, budgeting by paycheck and a 2027 savings challenge.
- [How to Price Handmade Items for a Christmas Market (With a Worked Example)](https://digitalworlds.cc/holiday/christmas-market-pricing/): A simple formula to price handmade gifts for Christmas markets and Etsy: materials, your time, overheads, fees and profit, with a worked candle example and a wholesale check.
- [New Year Budget Reset 2027: A 7-Step Checklist for January](https://digitalworlds.cc/holiday/new-year-budget-reset-2027/): Start 2027 with a clean money plan: total up December, list every bill, set a monthly budget, plan sinking funds, pick a debt strategy and set one savings goal. Free checklist.
- [52-Week Savings Challenge 2027: Start in January (Plans for €1k, €5k and €10k)](https://digitalworlds.cc/holiday/january-savings-challenge/): How the 52-week savings challenge works, three plans for 2027 (€1,378, €5,000 and €10,000) with weekly amounts, and how to make it stick past February.
- [How to Save €10,000 in 2027: A Month-by-Month Plan](https://digitalworlds.cc/holiday/save-10k-2027/): Saving €10,000 in a year means about €833 a month or €192 a week. Here is how to find that money, a month-by-month plan, and what to do if €10k is too much this year.
- [How to Budget by Paycheck (Biweekly Example That Stops the Payday Gap)](https://digitalworlds.cc/holiday/budget-by-paycheck/): Budget by paycheck instead of by month: assign each bill to the paycheck before its due date, save first, and stop running out before payday. Biweekly example included.
- [Free Notion Budget Template: 2 Ready-Made Budgets and How They Work](https://digitalworlds.cc/guides/notion-budget-template-free/): Two free Notion budget templates you can duplicate in one click: a category budget with planned vs spent, and a simple ADHD-friendly budget. Plus how the formulas work.
- [Notion Net Worth Tracker: Build One in 10 Minutes (Formula Included)](https://digitalworlds.cc/guides/notion-net-worth-tracker/): How to track your net worth in Notion: the database setup, the one formula that turns debts negative, a worked example and how to keep a monthly history.
- [Zero-Based Budget Example: Give Every Euro a Job (€2,600 Worked Example)](https://digitalworlds.cc/guides/zero-based-budget-example/): A zero-based budget worked example on €2,600 take-home pay: 16 envelopes, sinking funds and fun money, how to build one in 4 steps, and how it compares with 50/30/20.
- [Wedding Budget Breakdown by Category: Percentages + a €15,000 Example](https://digitalworlds.cc/guides/wedding-budget-breakdown/): A simple wedding budget breakdown by category with starting percentages, a worked €15,000 example for 80 guests, cost per guest, and 4 habits that keep the wedding on budget.
- [How Much Should Your Emergency Fund Be? Find Your Number in 5 Steps](https://digitalworlds.cc/guides/how-much-emergency-fund/): How big your emergency fund should be: add up only essential costs, choose 3 or 6 months, see how long it takes at €250 a month, and where to keep it. Worked example included.
- [How to Make a Bill Payment Calendar (and Stop Missing Due Dates)](https://digitalworlds.cc/guides/bill-payment-calendar/): Make a bill payment calendar in 4 steps: list every bill with due day and frequency, put them on a month view, tick them off as paid, and set aside for yearly bills. Example included.
- [How to Split Bills as a Couple: 50/50 vs By Income (Worked Example)](https://digitalworlds.cc/guides/split-bills-as-a-couple/): How couples can split shared bills fairly: 50/50 vs splitting by income, a worked example with €2,000 of shared costs, and a simple monthly settle-up system.
- [Credit Card Minimum Payments: Why They Take 9 Years (and How to Pay Off Faster)](https://digitalworlds.cc/guides/credit-card-minimum-payment/): Why paying only the credit card minimum takes years: a worked €3,000 at 22% APR example comparing minimum-only with fixed payments of €115, €150 and €200, plus 4 ways out.
- [52-Week Savings Challenge 2027: Classic, Reverse, €5,000 and €10,000 Versions](https://digitalworlds.cc/guides/52-week-savings-challenge/): How the 52-week savings challenge works: the classic €1,378 version, the reverse version, fixed weekly amounts for €5,000 or €10,000 in a year, and tips that make it stick.
- [How to Calculate Your Net Worth (Worked Example + What to Count)](https://digitalworlds.cc/guides/how-to-calculate-net-worth/): How to calculate your net worth: a worked example with assets and debts, the debt-to-asset ratio, what to count and leave out, and why to track it monthly.
- [Debt Payoff Colouring Chart: How the 100-Square Method Works](https://digitalworlds.cc/guides/debt-payoff-coloring-chart/): How a debt payoff colouring chart works: each square is 1% of your debt. Worked example with €6,400, why it keeps you motivated, and one chart vs one per debt.
- [How Much Does Etsy Take Per Sale? Fees Explained With a €20 Example](https://digitalworlds.cc/guides/etsy-fees-per-sale/): Etsy fees per sale explained: listing, transaction, payment processing and Offsite Ads, with a worked €20 example (13% normally, 28% with Offsite Ads) and 3 ways to keep more.
- [Freelance Bookkeeping Without an Accountant: What to Track Each Month](https://digitalworlds.cc/guides/freelance-bookkeeping-spreadsheet/): Simple freelance bookkeeping: invoices, expenses, VAT to pay and how much to set aside for tax, with a worked monthly example and a list of what to track.
- [How to Cut Your Wedding Guest List (and What 30 Fewer Guests Saves)](https://digitalworlds.cc/guides/cut-wedding-guest-list/): How to cut a wedding guest list without drama: the A/B/C list method, simple rules for plus-ones and kids, and a worked example of what 30 fewer guests saves.

## Polish (po polsku)

- [Limit działalności nierejestrowanej 2027: kalkulator](https://digitalworlds.cc/limit-dzialalnosci-nierejestrowanej-2027/): 2027 quarterly limit 11 137,50 zł (225% of the 4 950 zł minimum wage); free calculator of how much revenue is left this quarter.

- [Arkusz JDG 2027 (Excel): ZUS, składka zdrowotna, ryczałt czy liniowy](https://digitalworlds.cc/arkusz-jdg/): Arkusz Excel / Arkusze Google dla JDG: ewidencja przychodów i kosztów, ZUS pełny i preferencyjny, składka zdrowotna, zaliczki i porównanie ryczałt vs liniowy vs skala. 49 zł, pobierasz od razu.
- [Ryczałt czy liniowy? Porównanie na przykładzie freelancera](https://digitalworlds.cc/ryczalt-czy-liniowy/): Ryczałt 12%, podatek liniowy 19% czy skala 12/32%? Przykład dla JDG z 95 600 zł przychodu: ZUS, składka zdrowotna, podatek i ile zostaje na rękę.
- [Składka zdrowotna JDG 2026: ryczałt, liniowy i skala](https://digitalworlds.cc/skladka-zdrowotna-jdg/): Ile wynosi składka zdrowotna na JDG w 2026 r.? Ryczałt 498,35 / 830,58 / 1 495,04 zł, liniowy 4,9%, skala 9%, minimum 432,54 zł. Przykłady i kalkulator w arkuszu.
- [Klub Arkuszy: 39 arkuszy finansowych Excel i Google, nowe co miesiąc](https://digitalworlds.cc/klub/): Wszystkie arkusze finansowe w jednym abonamencie: budżet domowy, plan spłaty długów, cele oszczędnościowe, JDG 2027 (ZUS, podatek). 7 dni za darmo, potem 19 zł/mies. albo 149 zł za rok BLIK-iem.
- [Budżet domowy w Excelu: jak go zrobić w 20 minut (z gotowym szablonem)](https://digitalworlds.cc/budzet-domowy-excel/): Jak zrobić budżet domowy w Excelu lub Arkuszach Google krok po kroku: kategorie, plan vs wykonanie, zasada 50/30/20 i przykład dla rodziny. Gotowy szablon w Klubie Arkuszy.
- [Spłata długów: metoda kuli śnieżnej czy lawiny? Przykład z liczbami](https://digitalworlds.cc/kula-sniezna-czy-lawina/): Jak szybciej spłacić długi: metoda kuli śnieżnej (najmniejszy dług najpierw) czy lawiny (najwyższe oprocentowanie najpierw)? Przykład z kartą, debetem i kredytem gotówkowym oraz arkusz do planu spłaty.
- [Działalność nierejestrowana 2026: limit 10 813,50 zł na kwartał i zasady](https://digitalworlds.cc/dzialalnosc-nierejestrowana-limit-2026/): Działalność nierejestrowana w 2026 r.: kwartalny limit 10 813,50 zł (225% płacy minimalnej 4 806 zł), bez ZUS, ewidencja sprzedaży, podatek w PIT i co zrobić po przekroczeniu limitu.
- [Metoda kopertowa w Excelu: budżet kopertowy krok po kroku (przykład 6000 zł)](https://digitalworlds.cc/metoda-kopertowa/): Jak prowadzić budżet metodą kopertową w Excelu lub Arkuszach Google: przykład na 6000 zł netto, 10 kopert, 4 kroki i co zrobić, gdy w kopercie zabraknie pieniędzy.
- [Wyzwanie 52 tygodni 2027: ile uzbierasz (1378 zł, 6890 zł, 13780 zł)](https://digitalworlds.cc/wyzwanie-52-tygodni/): Wyzwanie oszczędnościowe 52 tygodni na 2027: wersja klasyczna (1378 zł), ×5 zł (6890 zł), ×10 zł (13780 zł) i odwrócona, plus 3 sposoby, żeby dotrwać do końca roku.
- [Darmowy arkusz budżetu domowego 2027 (Excel i Arkusze Google)](https://digitalworlds.cc/pl/): Darmowy budżet domowy 2027 po polsku, w złotówkach: metoda kopertowa, koperty roczne na OC, podatek i święta. Excel i Arkusze Google, bez rejestracji.
